messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: deploy pipeline triggered for release/2026-03-17 -> service=user-service. Canary targets: us-east-canary-a/us-east-canary-b/us-west-canary-a. Migration queued: 20260317_add_user_optin.sql.

incident-bot: Canary failure detected on us-east-canary-b: migration failed with lock timeout. Will not auto-promote.

db-oncall: I'm on the page. Pulling migration runner logs from canary-b.

claire-eng: What's the SQL? Any chance it's an application-level constraint?

db-oncall: Migration SQL: 
```sql
ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN opt_in boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false;
```
Postgres error: 
```
ERROR: could not obtain lock on relation "users"
DETAIL:  Process 91234 waits for ExclusiveLock; blocked by process 91230.
CONTEXT: ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN opt_in boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false
```

claire-eng: That pattern rings a bell: adding NOT NULL with DEFAULT triggers table rewrite on older PG and can hold an AccessExclusive lock. Bad for busy tables.

ops-bot: :information_source: Incident INC-2026-0317-db-mig created. Severity: P1. Paging db-oncall, tom-sre.

support-bot: 14 support tickets opened referencing write failures (500) starting ~4m after deploy start. Affected customers spiked in EU and APAC.

lisa-pm: We need blast radius and immediate action plan. Is read traffic impacted?

db-oncall: Reads unaffected. Writes that modify users are either timing out or erroring due to lock waits. Some background jobs that update user metadata are also failing.

claire-eng: Current options: A) kill the migration process on the failed canary and mark migration as ABORTED, B) roll back the whole deploy (stop other canaries), C) toggle feature-flag to block code paths that set opt_in. Which minimal-impact move?

tom-sre: Can we check other canaries' states? If some have applied the column, rolling back code might cause runtime errors if app expects the column. But usually adding a column is backward-compatible.

db-oncall: Querying migration_state table: us-east-canary-a: APPLIED, us-east-canary-b: IN_PROGRESS (stuck), us-west-canary-a: PENDING. So partial.

claire-eng: Partial apply. Rolling forward is risky because the stuck one might deadlock again. Rolling back release seems safest to stop further failures. But we should avoid destructive schema rollback.

lisa-pm: Decision: pause rollout and abort migration globally. Flip feature flag ff_opt_in to OFF to prevent new writes touching the column. Draft customer update.

claire-eng: Can devops flip FF immediately? I'll prep rollback job.

ops-bot: :gear: Initiating pause on release/2026-03-17. Canary promotions halted.

claire-eng: Toggling ff_opt_in -> OFF via flags API now.

ops-bot: :white_check_mark: ff_opt_in set to OFF. Telemetry watchers, please monitor write errors.

support-bot: Early signal: write errors down ~70%, but background migrator jobs still failing on a small subset.

db-oncall: I'm going to safely terminate the migration session on us-east-canary-b and check if the ALTER TABLE partially executed. If the session is killed, Postgres should rollback the DDL transaction.

db-oncall: Running: 
```sql
SELECT pid, state, query FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE query LIKE '%ALTER TABLE users%';
SELECT pg_terminate_backend(91234);
```

db-oncall: Termination returned true. Checking schema on canary-b: no opt_in column present. Good. Marking migration state for canary-b as FAILED.

claire-eng: What about canary-a where it succeeded? Any data implications? Column exists there and default was applied. That means schema is divergent across hosts. Need to ensure app code tolerates both.

tom-sre: App-level check: the new code path that writes opt_in is gated by ff_opt_in; with flag OFF, service on canary-a will not write to the new column. So safe to stop the release and leave opt_in present where it is.

db-oncall: I'm updating migration coordinator to set migration 20260317_add_user_optin -> ABORTED globally so workers won't attempt it.

ops-bot: :lock: Release paused and migration aborted globally. Rollback plan: stop deployment, do not attempt schema removal.

lisa-pm: Customer comms: "We've paused today's release due to a partially-applied database schema change that caused write errors for some customers. We've stopped the rollout and mitigated most user-impact by toggling the feature flag. We'll follow up with a detailed timeline within 1 hour."

support-bot: Sent initial customer message to affected accounts.

claire-eng: Follow-up tasks: run fleet-wide schema audit to enumerate nodes with/without the column; ensure no replicas are mid-migration; schedule a safe maintenance window for schema change using add-column NULL + backfill + set not null.

db-oncall: Fleet audit results: hosts with opt_in: us-east-canary-a, prod-db-7. Hosts without: us-east-canary-b, us-west-canary-a, prod-db-6. So mixed state.

tom-sre: Recommendation: keep schema where present, avoid destructive DROP COLUMN. Plan safer migration: 1) ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN opt_in boolean, no default, NULLABLE; 2) backfill in small batches using update with LIMIT; 3) once backfill done, set NOT NULL and add default in a maintenance window. Also add migration guard to avoid running on busy hosts.

lisa-pm: Agreed. Also add automation to detect DDL that will cause table rewrites and fail canary fast.

claire-eng: I'll open a ticket for migration-runbook updates and add a checklist: DB owner review, backfill script, rate limits, feature flag gating.

ops-bot: :white_check_mark: Rollback job rb-20260317-01 completed: deploy halted, traffic reverted where applicable.

tom-sre: Handoff: I'll watch metrics for 30 minutes then hand to db-oncall for overnight. db-oncall, you're primary now.

db-oncall: Taking over. I'll run hourly checks on pg_locks and migration_state and escalate if new errors.

support-bot: Monitoring for new tickets. Will notify customers if situation worsens.

lisa-pm: Next status update in 45 minutes or sooner if critical. Postmortem to be scheduled with eng, db, and SRE tomorrow.

incident-bot: INC-2026-0317-db-mig status set to monitoring.

claire-eng: Closing thread for now; keeping channel open for runbook and remediation work."
